english: and let $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $g(x)=\max\{f(t):x-1\le t\le x\}$. Let $S$ be the set of all points of the interval $(0,5)$ at which $g$ is not differentiable. Then the sum of all the elements of $S$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ इस प्रकार परिभाषित है

तथा माना कि $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=\max\{f(t):x-1\le t\le x\}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। माना कि $S$ अन्तराल $(0,5)$ के उन सभी बिन्दुओं का समुच्चय है जिन पर $g$ अवकलनीय नहीं है। तब $S$ के सभी अवयवों का योग ______ है।
solution: $f$ increases on $(-\infty,1]$ to $f(1)=1$, decreases on $[1,2]$ to $0$, then increases linearly with slope $\frac32$
Junctions: at $x=1$ and $x=2$ both one-sided derivatives are $0$; at $x=3$ the same line continues. At $x=\frac52$: left derivative $-2u=-1$, right derivative $\frac32$: corner
solution_full: Shape of $f$: for $t\le2$, $f(t)=1-(t-1)^{2}$, increasing on $(-\infty,1]$, maximum $1$ at $t=1$, decreasing on $[1,2]$ with $f(2)=0$. For $t>2$, $f(t)=\frac32(t-2)$ is increasing and $f$ is continuous at $2$.
Case $1\le x\le2$: the window contains $t=1$, the global maximum point of $f$ on $(-\infty,2]$, and $[x-1,x]\subset(-\infty,2]$. So $g(x)=1$.

Case $2\le x\le3$: on $[x-1,2]\subset[1,2]$, $f$ decreases, so its maximum is $f(x-1)=1-(x-2)^{2}$; on $(2,x]$ the maximum is $f(x)=\frac32(x-2)$. Hence $g(x)=\max\left\{1-(x-2)^{2},\frac32(x-2)\right\}$.
With $u=x-2\in[0,1]$: $1-u^{2}\ge\frac32u\iff 2u^{2}+3u-2\le0\iff(2u-1)(u+2)\le0\iff u\le\frac12$. So $g=1-(x-2)^{2}$ on $\left[2,\frac52\right]$ and $g=\frac32(x-2)$ on $\left[\frac52,3\right]$.

Check the junctions. $x=1$: $g'(1^{-})=2-2=0$ and $g'(1^{+})=0$. $x=2$: $g'(2^{-})=0$ and $g'(2^{+})=-2(x-2)\big|_{x=2}=0$. $x=3$: the formula $\frac32(x-2)$ is the same on both sides. So $g$ is differentiable at $1,2,3$.
$x=\frac52$: $g'\left(\frac52^{-}\right)=-2\cdot\frac12=-1$ and $g'\left(\frac52^{+}\right)=\frac32$. These differ, so $g$ is not differentiable at $\frac52$.
Inside each case $g$ is a polynomial, so $S=\left\{\frac52\right\}$ and the required sum is $2.50$.
originality_note: New: a sliding-window maximum g(x) = max f on [x-1, x] of a piecewise function with a hump and a rising tail; the window max is flat over the hump, smooth at the regime changes, and has a single corner where the trailing end of the hump and the leading end of the line tie (way 2: function of a moving interval). Closest known: g(x) = max{f(t): 0 <= t <= x} (running max from a fixed left end, as in JEE Main 2021). Different because: the window has fixed length, so the left end matters and the tie f(x-1) = f(x) creates the corner, while the apparent junctions 1, 2, 3 are smooth.
key_step: Split by the position of the window: g = f(x), then 1, then max{f(x-1), f(x)}, then f(x); the only corner is the tie x = 5/2.
justification: An unfamiliar construction (moving-window max) requiring four regimes and a check of each junction, with a numerical answer; the algebra is light. Placed with 2024-P1-Q17 (L3) and above the running-max JEE Main problems.

concept_use.Continuity and Differentiability of func: g is a maximum over a moving window; in the third regime it is max{f(x-1), f(x)}, which has a corner at the tie x = 5/2.
f is defined by different formulas for t <= 2 and t > 2; which piece supplies the maximum decides the formula of g in each regime.

stem_review: Read as a student: f and g have domain and codomain, the window [x-1, x] is closed, S is on the open interval (0,5), one reading. Checked by a fine numerical scan of g that the only non-smooth point in (0,5) is 2.5. Answer 2.50, a positive decimal. Changed: No change.
